headline: Student Election Candidate Suspends Campaign To Complete Mandatory Three-Week 'De-Escalation' Workshop In Origami
body:
Rahul Varma, a candidate for a central panel seat in the Delhi University student elections, has officially paused his final-day door-to-door campaigning to attend a court-mandated three-week intensive workshop on the delicate art of paper-folding. The directive, aimed at curbing the competitive spirit of election season, requires all candidates to demonstrate an ability to fold a swan without crushing it in a fit of partisan rage before they are permitted to attend the official vote counting.

“My campaign manager was worried about our momentum, but honestly, the swan is much harder than the candidate manifesto,” said Varma while squinting at a complex crease pattern. “The High Court was very clear: if the campus environment doesn’t look like a meditation retreat by tomorrow morning, the counting is off. I’ve already traded my megaphone for a set of bamboo folders and a stack of eco-friendly construction paper. It’s significantly quieter for the neighbors.”

Election officials have confirmed that candidates who successfully produce a stable origami crane will be granted an ‘Inner Peace’ certification, which serves as the new gatekeeper for participation in the tallying process. As of this morning, at least six major party candidates have been spotted in the library basement, aggressively whispering soothing mantras while attempting to balance paper wings, with several reported cases of high-stakes paper cuts slowing down the process.
caption: Forget aggressive manifestos; it’s all about the perfect paper crease now. Can a swan save the vote count? #DUSU #DelhiUniversity #OrigamiDiplomacy #StudentPolitics (satire)
igHook: Tag a candidate who definitely wouldn't have the patience to fold a paper swan.
imagePrompt: A close-up of a stack of colorful construction paper on a wooden desk, with a partially folded, slightly crumpled origami bird sitting next to a pile of campaign pamphlets.

sourceHeadline.title: DUSU polls: Delhi HC directs DU, Police to act against hooligans by tomorrow or vote counting will be stayed

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 0 excels by grounding an absurd bureaucratic mandate (origami as a prerequisite for election participation) in specific, vivid details like 'Inner Peace' certification and the mental image of candidates aggressively whispering mantras. It balances the required structural AP tone with genuine warmth and originality, avoiding the repetitive 'apology note/painting over posters' trope that plagued many other submissions in this batch.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses a fictional student candidate name (Rahul Varma) which is a common name and does not target a specific real individual. The satire focuses on the absurdity of election regulations rather than harming any real public figures, groups, or communities. The image prompt is generic and free of restricted content.
